question: The ongoing review of the Generalised Scheme of Preferences (GSP) Regulation has raised several questions about the application of the automatic safeguard clause. This clause is a responsive mechanism for GSP beneficiary countries that temporarily suspends tariff preferences when a certain import threshold has been exceeded.

At this stage, it has not been clearly established whether the clause will apply only to standard GSP beneficiary countries, or whether it will also concern countries with GSP+ status. Similarly, making 6% of EU imports the threshold that triggers the clause has been mentioned, but not officially confirmed.

Can the Commission clarify whether the automatic safeguard clause provided for in the new GSP Regulation will also apply to GSP+ countries, and whether the proposed 6% of EU imports is the threshold that will be used to trigger it?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.11.2025) The trilogue discussion on the review of the Generalised Scheme Preferences (GSP) regulation is still ongoing and therefore, it is not possible to anticipate the result of that negotiation.

The relevant provision in the Commission legislative proposal of 21 September 20211 is largely based on the provisions currently in force2 establishing an automatic suspension of preferences for certain textile and agricultural products when the total value of such imports from a specific beneficiary country exceeds the relevant share of total GSP imports during a calendar year.

The suspension would not apply to countries with a share of relevant product not exceeding a share of 6% of total EU imports of the same products. These provisions would apply both to standard GSP and Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) beneficiary countries.
